bib.title: MoE-LLaVA: Mixture of Experts for Large Vision-Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; routing-plot axis text (Figs 4-14) is plot residue only.

question: How can a Mixture-of-Experts sparse architecture be trained for a large vision-language model without the performance degradation seen when converting an LLM to an LVLM and sparsifying at once?
hypothesis: Initialising the experts from a dense LVLM (stage II FFN weights) lets the sparse model transition gradually and avoids degradation (implied by the three-stage MoE-Tuning design).
contributions: MoE-Tuning, a three-stage training strategy for adapting MoE to LVLMs and preventing degradation caused by sparsity
MoE-LLaVA, a MoE-based sparse LVLM framework that expands parameters while keeping computational cost
Experiments showing multi-modal understanding and hallucination mitigation with about 3B sparse activated parameters

method.summary: LLaVA-1.5-style LVLM (CLIP-Large/336 encoder, 2-layer MLP projector, small LLM backbones) trained in three stages: MLP only, full LLM as dense LVLM, then FFNs replicated into 4 experts with a top-2 linear softmax router and only the FFN/MoE layers trained. MoE layers replace FFNs in alternating layers; load-balancing auxiliary loss with alpha 0.01.

training.objective: auto-regressive loss on generated text only plus alpha times load-balancing auxiliary loss (Fedus et al., 2022); Ltotal = Lregressive + alpha*Laux
training.batch_size: 256 (stage I), 128 (stages II and III); 32/16/16 per GPU
training.regularisation: load-balancing auxiliary loss, alpha 0.01; Batch Priority Routing with capacity 1.5
training.hardware: 8 x A800-80G for main results; ablation timings on 8 x V100-32G
training.wall_clock: Ablation timings on 8 V100-32G (Qwen-1.8B x4 default config): 20h FFN-only tuning, 27h all-parameter tuning; top-k 1 19h, top-k 2 20h; 'All' MoE layers 32h; 1 expert 13h, 2 experts 14h

other.deepspeed: Zero2 stages I and II, Zero2 offload stage III
other.stability: fp16 sometimes gives NaN loss; authors note training stability difficulty with 16-bit float
other.stage_trainable: Stage I MLP only; Stage II all LLM parameters (VE excluded); Stage III FFN/MoE layers only (Table 5a 'FFN' = all FFN and MoE layers)

parameters.router: linear layer W in R^(D x E) with softmax, top-k

limits: Authors concede training stability difficulties, particularly with 16-bit float precision.
OpenChat-7B x4 MoE is worse than dense; authors speculate the 655k multimodal instruction data is insufficient for 10B-level sparsification and leave it to future work.
Ablation tables do not name the backbone, report one run, no seeds or variance.
Optimizer and warmup are not stated; step counts not stated.
Table 3 marks some results with training-data overlap (asterisk) for VQAv2 and GQA.
Text deltas against LLaVA-1.5 do not always match the table values.
Broader impacts: false information, bias, over-reliance.
